boxes.box: `main` contains the foundation; `git ls-files` shows no build output, and a secret scan of the tree is clean
boxes.evidence: Clone and canonical .git/refs/heads/main both = a8d8f31bf16b41cdaedcfaf42db06930173068cd. `git ls-files` (313 paths) lists apps/mobile, packages/domain, supabase (14 migrations, config.toml, seed.sql, development-catalogue.sql), scripts/backend, the workflow and the lockfile. It has no dist*/, .expo/, build/, coverage/, supabase/.temp, supabase/.branches, node_modules or .env* except apps/mobile/.env.example, whose key is empty. .gitignore:10-24 covers these paths. My own pattern scan of the tracked tree found no sb_secret_/sb_publishable_ values, JWTs, PEM keys, AWS/GitHub/OpenAI/Slack tokens or literal secret assignments. config.toml secrets are env() references. The backend scripts read keys from `supabase status` at runtime and create random UUID passwords. The coordinator's Gitleaks result of 306 files is stated only in the handoff; bootstrap-gates.md:16 records an earlier 301-file run.

boxes.box: On a fresh clone of `main`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check` and (local Supabase running) `pnpm backend:test` pass; result lines are in the handoff
boxes.evidence: Run in /private/tmp/fitlog-qa1-main-a8d8f31. `rtk proxy pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` → 'Lockfile is up to date… Done in 1.3s using pnpm v10.27.0'. `rtk proxy pnpm check` → domain 'pass 10 fail 0'; mobile 'Test Suites: 7 passed, 7 total / Tests: 126 passed, 126 total'; planner 'pass 22 fail 0'; tsc, eslint --max-warnings=0 and design rules pass; 'plan.json and board.html match GOALS.md'. `rtk proxy pnpm backend:test` → all four suites print the same 'passed' lines as handoff.md:37-41. The configured seed (config.toml:72 sql_paths includes development-catalogue.sql, which contains exercise 20000000-…0001) satisfies verify.mjs:39-40 without a manual seed. scripts/backend contains no rtk call.

boxes.box: Android and iOS JavaScript exports pass from the same clone
boxes.evidence: `rtk proxy pnpm --filter @fitlog/mobile exec expo export --platform ios --platform android --output-dir .expo/export-native` in the same clone → 'ios bundles (1): …entry-69fef94d….hbc (4.5MB)', 'android bundles (1): …entry-b6ebb81e….hbc (4.8MB)', 'Exported: .expo/export-native'. These are JS/Hermes exports only, not native or release builds.

boxes.box: Review reports are in `docs/evidence/QA-1/`, and every finding left open names its owning goal
boxes.evidence: The reports are present in the canonical docs/evidence/QA-1/: bootstrap-code-review.md, bootstrap-security-review.md, auth-callback-fix.md, auth-callback-verification.md, bootstrap-reproducibility-fix.md, portability.md and bootstrap-gates.md. F-1 is closed in source: auth-callback.ts:18-41 does an exact prefix match, refuses fragments, accepts a single code and refuses while signed in; there is no supabase setSession in apps/mobile/src; supabase.ts:9 sets pkce and detectSessionInUrl:false. G-1 is fixed (config.toml:72). R-1 is fixed (config.toml:164-171; AuthScreen.tsx:5,22 uses AUTH_CALLBACK_PATH). C-1–C-5, F-2–F-8h, R-2/R-3 and the F-ups name later goals. However, bootstrap-security-review.md:195 F-8i (scripts/backend/preview-account.mjs:15 hard-codes the macOS-only path /private/tmp/fitlog-preview-account.json) names its owner as 'QA-1 portability note'.
